summary: S_multiphase_wetting_domains returned four usable abstracts and one excluded record. S3 supports only the broad relation that RNA sequence/structure/modifications correlate with RNA crowding/condensate behavior; S1 is a protein-context relation about composition/miscibility and molecular/environmental modulation. S2 is general crowding; S4 concerns coacervate protocell growth/division. None states a relation connecting RNA mixture partitioning to internal dilute-domain nucleation or persistence, so G_mix_to_internal_domain remains open and the bridge remains a hypothesis. C05 ran successfully but is illustrative, not fitted: for fixed x it gives q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), r=kf*max(x-xc,0), and the carryover model has identical q dynamics under matched effective r. Thus observed q(t) cannot distinguish the causal driver; a matched factorial composition/carryover perturbation is needed. Evidence refs: S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S1-S4, C05, C01-C04, E02, initial_measurements.json.

S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S1 abstract review describes protein condensate composition/miscibility responding to molecular or environmental changes; this is protein context and does not establish an RNA cavity mechanism.

S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S2 abstract discusses general molecular crowding without a partition-to-cavity relation; S4 discusses coacervate protocell compartmentalization/growth/division, not cavities inside transcribing RNA droplets.

equations: Unclosed phenomenological model: dq/dt=kf*max(x-xc,0)*(qmax-q)-kc*q. It does not derive x(t), thermodynamics, or internal topology.
For fixed x and kc>0, r=kf*max(x-xc,0), q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), and q(t)=q*+(q0-q*)exp(-(r+kc)t). If x<=xc, r=0 and q(t)=q0*exp(-kc*t), with decay half-life ln(2)/kc.
Carryover alternative: dq/dt=kg*max(c-cc,0)*(qmax-q)-kc*q. If kg*max(c-cc,0)=kf*max(x-xc,0), trajectories are identical; q(t) alone cannot identify the driver.
For a measured phase species i, Ki=Ci,dense/Ci,dilute only when the dilute concentration is positive; no supported mapping from Ki to q.

parameters_ranges.kf: positive h^-1; unmeasured; C05 used illustrative 0.1-10 h^-1
parameters_ranges.kc: positive h^-1; unmeasured; C05 used illustrative 0.001-0.1 h^-1
parameters_ranges.x: [0,1]; C05 grid {0,0.1,0.25,0.5,1} is illustrative, not observed

candidates.initial_boundary_conditions: q(0) observed around 0.014 in A and B; x(0), phase geometry and interfaces are unknown. No spatial condition is specified, so this is not a spatially closed model.
candidates.observation_mapping: q maps only to the supplied mean per-object segmented empty-area fraction. It is not concentration, volume fraction, or ratio of total dark area to total filled area. x, c, and time-varying phase concentrations are unmeasured.
alternatives: Carryover or other reaction conditions drive a global phase-state change; the same mathematical form explains q(t).
Population turnover, field sampling, or segmentation changes mean q while individual cavity state is stable; tracking does not establish within-droplet cavity trajectories.
predictions: At matched carryover and total RNA, titrating measured RNA mixture fraction should shift q onset/steady state if composition is causal; fixed x above xc predicts q* increasing with x and below xc predicts decay toward zero.

Factorially vary composition and measured carryover. A pure composition mechanism predicts residual composition dependence under matched carryover; a pure carryover mechanism predicts response to carryover at fixed composition. Matching effective rates explains why observational q(t) alone cannot discriminate.
If q rises while x is constant, the specific changing-composition driver is weakened; after x falls below xc, this model predicts exponential relaxation with half-life ln(2)/kc.
checks: C05 executed, returncode 0, stderr empty; it was an illustrative conditional calculation, not a fit or physical estimate.
Analytical fixed-driver solution has units dq/dt=h^-1; r,kf,kc are h^-1 and x,xc,q,qmax are dimensionless.
For nonnegative rates, q*=qmax*r/(r+kc) is in [0,qmax]; x<=xc gives q*=0 for kc>0; kc->0 at r>0 gives q*->qmax; kf=0 gives exponential decay.
C05 carryover checks gave identical effective rates in both examples; values of c and cc are arbitrary illustrative units, not measured chemical concentrations.

C05 code checked qss against the global max qmax=0.5, not each grid row individual qmax; the closed-form formula itself guarantees qss<=the selected qmax. No temporal integration or comparison to measured q was performed.
C04 tie-line 0 variant partition ratio is undefined because both dilute and dense concentrations are zero.
evidence_conflicts: E02 is compatible with a mixture effect but is not a controlled dose-response and does not measure RNA composition over time.
C04 endpoint partitions and abstract literature do not explain internal geometry, nucleation, or persistence.
A/B are confounded by possible carryover; q is an image metric and tracking does not identify persistent within-droplet cavity state.

dissent: C05 is valid as a conditional ODE calculation, but its parameter ranges are intentionally broad and the global-bound check is weaker than checking each row against its own qmax; the analytical bound resolves that mathematical point. It supplies no empirical mechanism evidence.
